title: Why she took up the valve trombone
summary: She wanted an instrument to play; seeing Bob Brookmeyer and Billy Eckstine, she chose valve trombone and Cliff found one at Manny's.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Let me ask you something that kind of leads out to that. One of the cool
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
school modern musicians, who I guess was making a name for himself in the 1950's was Bob Brookmeyer. Bob was a valve trombone player.
Yes.
Did that have any influence on your decision to take up that instrument?
No.

The reason that I took up the valve trombone was because I had seen this -- I had been out to California -- out of Hawaii, rather, and I was working in a place where on Sunday they had jam sessions. And a gal came in there who was a musician, one of the early jazz musicians. I think she was a retiree from Ina Ray Hutton's band. But anyway, she sang a couple of songs, and then afterwards, she picked up the trumpet and played. When I came back, I said, "You know, that's a good idea." Because after a singer has sung a couple of songs, what do you do for encore? So I said to Cliff, "I think I want to

play a horn, find an instrument." I didn't want to play the trumpet, because I figured it was too hard.
And I didn't want to play the trombone -- the slide trombone -- because I figured my arms weren't long enough. And I would look like a circus act.
So, it dawned on me that Billy Eckstine, when he had a big band, he played the valve trombone.
Incidentally, how tall are you?
I'm four feet-eleven.
Just uh -- of course, I know the answer to that question. (Inaudible).
Yeah, right.

And so I said to Cliff, "Look, I think I'd like a valve trombone." He was working downtown at the time at Ryan's and I said, "If you're anywhere near Manny's" -- Manny's is a music shop downtown where all the guys get their instruments and accessories and et cetera -- "tell Manny that I'll be interested in a valve trombone."
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrk 2-2915 WOrk 2-2943
So Cliff, you know, he went along with anything. He went by Manny's and said, "Look, Manny, Maxine wants a valve trombone."
And Manny said, "A guy walked in here yesterday with his valve trombone. He wants sixty-five dollars for it."
So Cliff came home and told me about it. I said, "Grab it!"
That was a good price.
